On Wed, Apr 21, 2027 at 09:22 Aditya Rao wrote:
> Monica (SRE) — can you confirm whether the recent prefix-eviction change that shipped last night could be the cause?

Quick update from SRE triage: we confirmed a sharp rise in KV miss rates correlated with the release of the "prefix-eviction-v2" heuristic deployed at 02:10 PT. Preliminary evidence:
- KV cache miss ratio for high-cardinality prefixes rose from ~6% baseline to ~47% between 08:45-09:10.
- p95 handler time for /v1/generate increased from 120ms to ~1.85s during the spike.
- The burst pattern matches a cascading eviction: eviction policy prunes shared prefix entries aggressively, causing upstream requests to repopulate caches and trigger head-of-line blocking in the batching queue. That, in turn, produced queue backlog -> connection timeouts and 504 upstream responses.

Immediate mitigations taken:
1) Initiated rollback of prefix-eviction-v2 by tag (rolling back across 3 availability zones).
2) Enabled per-tenant cache bypass for Parkway to force direct model memory fetch (reduces cache churn while rollback completes).
3) Raised batch worker parallelism temporarily to reduce coalescence delay.

We’re watching stabilization metrics (KV miss ratio, batch queue depth, model GPU utilization). If rollback finishes cleanly we should see error rate return to baseline within 30–45 minutes. I’ve attached the Grafana snapshot of the KV miss curve.

Attachment: grafana_kv_miss_p95.png

— Monica (oncall SRE)

Subject: RE: Intermittent 504s and timeouts on /v1/generate (resolved)

Sierra — follow-up and summary:

What happened:
- A recently deployed prefix-eviction heuristic (prefix-eviction-v2) aggressively pruned shared cache entries for high-cardinality prefixes. That caused a cascade of cache repopulation traffic which saturated the batching queue and produced timeouts/504s for some requests.

What we did:
- Rolled back prefix-eviction-v2 at 14:40 PT on 2027-04-22.
- Applied a Parkway tenant-level bypass and increased worker parallelism while we monitored trend lines.
- Implemented a short-term patch to throttle prefix repopulation (rate limiter on repopulating hot prefixes).

Result:
- Error rate for /v1/generate returned to baseline within ~22 minutes after the rollback. Live chat flows stabilized and batch scoring resumed normal windowing.

Next steps / postmortem plan:
- We’ll publish a full postmortem by EOD tomorrow that includes RCA, code diff for the eviction heuristic, test gaps, and remediation (stricter canary thresholds + synthetic workloads for prefix-heavy patterns).
- CS will coordinate any credit/financial remediation with Parkway (Lauren).

Links / attachments:
- Postmortem (draft): https://drive.redwood.example/postmortems/prefix-eviction-fanout-20270422.docx
- Incident dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/ops/kv-cache-metrics
- Rollback plan (internal): proposed_rollback_plan.pdf

If you’d like a sync with our engineering and SRE leads we can set up a brief 30-minute call. Apologies again for the disruption — we’re prioritizing preventing recurrence.

— Aditya Rao
Head of North America Accounts, Redwood Inference
